summary: pack_exchange_kokkos writes each migrating atom's shear history into the send buffer at an offset derived from the atom's LOCAL INDEX instead of its slot in the send list, so the bytes actually transmitted are uninitialized memory (and the write can run past the end of the buffer).
evidence: fix_wall_gran_kokkos.cpp:368-374 'void ...operator()(TagFixWallGranPackExchange, const int &mysend) const { const int i = d_sendlist(mysend); int m = i*size_history; for (int v = 0; v < size_history; v++) d_buf(m++) = static_cast<double>(d_history_one(i,v)); ...' - the offset must be 'mysend*size_history'.  The receiving side proves it: fix_wall_gran_kokkos.cpp:418-425 uses 'int m = i*size_history;' with i the RECEIVE SLOT, and src/KOKKOS/comm_kokkos.cpp:1373-1410 sends exactly the first 'nextrasend' doubles of k_buf_send, where nextrasend is this function's return value 'nsend*size_history' (fix_wall_gran_kokkos.cpp:410).  comm_kokkos.cpp:1371 only guarantees 'nsend*fix_iextra->maxexchange' doubles of capacity, so writing at d_sendlist(mysend)*size_history (an index up to nlocal*size_history) both scatters the data outside the transmitted window and can overrun the buffer.  The sibling styles index by the send slot: fix_spring_self_kokkos.cpp:187 'int m = nsend + offset;' with 'd_buf[mysend] = m;', and fix_wall_flow_kokkos.cpp:224 'd_buf(mysend) = ...'.
failure_scenario: multi-processor granular run with 'fix wall/gran/kk hooke/history ...': on the first timestep an atom in contact with the wall migrates to another rank, its tangential shear history arrives as whatever happened to be in buffer slots 0..nsend*3-1, so the frictional force jumps discontinuously; with nlocal*size_history larger than the send buffer it is an out-of-bounds device write (silent corruption or a GPU segfault).
suggested_fix: Change 'int m = i*size_history;' to 'int m = mysend*size_history;' in TagFixWallGranPackExchange.

summary: unpack_exchange_kokkos stores the received shear history at the receive-slot index instead of the destination atom index returned by d_indices, so the history is written onto the wrong atoms and the migrated atoms keep stale history.
evidence: fix_wall_gran_kokkos.cpp:418-426 'int index = d_indices(i); if (index > -1) { int m = i*size_history; for (int v = 0; v < size_history; v++) d_history_one(i,v) = static_cast<KK_FLOAT>(d_buf(m++)); }' - the guard reads d_indices(i) but the destination is 'd_history_one(i,v)' rather than 'd_history_one(index,v)'.  Every other KOKKOS fix that implements this hook uses the mapped index: fix_wall_flow_kokkos.cpp:276 'd_current_segment(index) = static_cast<int>(d_buf(i));', fix_spring_self_kokkos.cpp:261-263 'd_xoriginal(index,0) = ...', fix_ti_spring_kokkos.cpp:252-254.  d_indices is filled by AtomVecKokkos::unpack_exchange_kokkos (comm_kokkos.cpp:1358-1359) and gives the local index the i-th received atom was placed at, which is generally != i.
failure_scenario: multi-processor 'fix wall/gran/kk hooke/history' run: after an exchange the received atoms' d_history_one entries are left at whatever the (compacted) local slot held, while the low-numbered local atoms 0..nrecv-1 - which did not migrate - have their tangential displacement history overwritten with other atoms' values.  Friction forces are wrong for both sets of particles and the error accumulates because the history is integrated over time.
suggested_fix: Write 'd_history_one(index,v) = static_cast<KK_FLOAT>(d_buf(m++));'.

summary: post_force silently does nothing for pairstyle 'granular' (and for wallstyle 'region'): the if/else chain has no branch and no error for them, so the wall exerts no force at all.
evidence: fix_wall_gran_kokkos.cpp:107-119 'if (pairstyle == HOOKE) error->all(...); else if (pairstyle == HOOKE_HISTORY) { ... } else if (pairstyle == HERTZ_HISTORY) error->all(...);' - there is no branch for the fourth style.  The base class header src/KOKKOS/fix_wall_gran_old.h:29 declares 'enum { HOOKE, HOOKE_HISTORY, HERTZ_HISTORY, GRANULAR };' so 'fix wall/gran/kk granular ...' (accepted by FixWallGranOld's constructor, src/KOKKOS/fix_wall_gran_old.cpp:81 'else if (strcmp(arg[3],"granular") == 0) pairstyle = GRANULAR;') leaves pairstyle == 3 and falls off the end of the chain.  The file's own shadowing enum at fix_wall_gran_kokkos.cpp:24 'enum{HOOKE,HOOKE_HISTORY,HERTZ_HISTORY,BONDED_HISTORY};' hides this: value 3 is named BONDED_HISTORY there and is never tested.  The same hole exists in the inner chain: fix_wall_gran_kokkos.cpp:110-117 dispatches only XPLANE/YPLANE/ZPLANE/ZCYLINDER, so wallstyle REGION (fix_wall_gran_old.cpp:379) launches no kernel either.
failure_scenario: 'fix wall/gran/kk granular hertz/material ... tangential mindlin ...' (or any hooke/history wall attached to a region) runs to completion with no error message and zero wall force - particles pass straight through the wall, while the plain 'fix wall/gran' gives the correct granular contact forces.
suggested_fix: Add a final 'else error->all(FLERR, "Fix wall/gran/kk does not yet support ... style");' to both the pairstyle and the wallstyle chain, and rename the third enumerator in fix_wall_gran_kokkos.cpp to GRANULAR so it matches fix_wall_gran_old.h.

summary: The device hooke/history kernel omits the limit_damping clamp on the normal force, so the 'limit_damping' keyword is silently ignored by fix wall/gran/kk.
evidence: fix_wall_gran_kokkos.cpp:226-227 'KK_FLOAT damp = meff*gamman_kk*vnnr*rsqinv; KK_FLOAT ccel = kn_kk*(radius-r)*rinv - damp;' goes straight on to the tangential terms.  The CPU original has one more line at src/KOKKOS/fix_wall_gran_old.cpp:897-899: 'damp = meff*gamman*vnnr*rsqinv; ccel = kn*(radius-r)*rinv - damp; if (limit_damping && (ccel < 0.0)) ccel = 0.0;'.  limit_damping is a real command-line option parsed at fix_wall_gran_old.cpp:120-123 ('if (strcmp(arg[iarg],"limit_damping") == 0) { limit_damping = 1; iarg += 1; }') and is a plain int member (fix_wall_gran_old.h:72) that the functor copy already carries.  Every other line of the kernel matches hooke_history() exactly.
failure_scenario: 'fix wall/gran/kk hooke/history kn kt gamman gammat xmu 1 limit_damping zplane ...': for fast approaches where the damping term exceeds the elastic term, ccel stays negative and the wall pulls the particle in (and the tangential Coulomb limit fn = xmu*|ccel*r| is computed from the unclamped value), whereas the CPU fix clamps it to zero.
suggested_fix: Add 'if (limit_damping && (ccel < static_cast<KK_FLOAT>(0.0))) ccel = 0.0;' after the ccel assignment in the kernel.

summary: The Kokkos overrides of grow_arrays and copy_arrays handle only history_one and drop the array_atom half, and maxexchange is set to size_history, so the 'contacts' option leaves array_atom never regrown while the inherited pack/unpack_exchange still read and write size_peratom_cols entries of it.
evidence: fix_wall_gran_kokkos.cpp:303-311 'void FixWallGranKokkos<DeviceType>::grow_arrays(int nmax) { if (use_history) { ... memoryKK->grow_kokkos(k_history_one,history_one,nmax,size_history,...); ... } }' and :316-323 copy_arrays likewise only wraps the history part.  The base versions do both: src/KOKKOS/fix_wall_gran_old.cpp:1567-1573 'if (use_history) memory->grow(history_one,...); if (peratom_flag) { memory->grow(array_atom,nmax,size_peratom_cols,"fix_wall_gran_old:array_atom"); }' and :1579-1588 copy_arrays copies array_atom too.  The KOKKOS pack_exchange/unpack_exchange delegate to the base (fix_wall_gran_kokkos.cpp:348, :356), which writes 'size_history + size_peratom_cols' doubles when peratom_flag (fix_wall_gran_old.cpp:1609-1625), yet the constructor sets 'maxexchange = size_history;' (fix_wall_gran_kokkos.cpp:35).  'contacts' is a supported keyword (fix_wall_gran_old.cpp:410-412 'peratom_flag = 1; size_peratom_cols = 8;').  On top of that the device kernel never fills array_atom and never calls clear_stored_contacts(), which the CPU post_force does (fix_wall_gran_old.cpp:637-639, 713-722).
failure_scenario: 'fix 1 all wall/gran/kk hooke/history ... zplane 0 NULL contacts': array_atom is allocated once (in the base constructor at the initial atom->nmax) and never grown, so as soon as atoms are added or nmax grows, copy_arrays/pack_exchange index past the end of it (heap corruption); and even before that, the per-atom contact output is always the stale/zero content the kernel never writes.
suggested_fix: Call FixWallGranOld::grow_arrays()/copy_arrays() for the peratom_flag part from the Kokkos overrides, set maxexchange to size_history + (peratom_flag ? size_peratom_cols : 0), and either fill array_atom in the kernel or reject the 'contacts' keyword in FixWallGranKokkos::init().

summary: The exchange hooks of fix wall/gran/kk are missing three of the sync/modify calls their sibling styles perform: no modify<DeviceType>() after pack_exchange_kokkos writes the device history, no sync<DeviceType>() before the unpack kernel, and no sync_host() before the host unpack_exchange.
evidence: fix_wall_gran_kokkos.cpp:386-411 pack_exchange_kokkos does 'k_history_one.template sync<DeviceType>();' and then runs a kernel that WRITES d_history_one (the copylist compaction at :375-380 'd_history_one(i,v) = d_history_one(j,v);'), but never calls 'k_history_one.template modify<DeviceType>();' - compare fix_spring_self_kokkos.cpp:240 and fix_ti_spring_kokkos.cpp:231 and fix_wall_flow_kokkos.cpp:257, which all do.  fix_wall_gran_kokkos.cpp:431-450 unpack_exchange_kokkos writes the device view and calls modify<DeviceType>() (:449) without a preceding sync<DeviceType>() - compare fix_spring_self_kokkos.cpp:286 and fix_ti_spring_kokkos.cpp:277.  fix_wall_gran_kokkos.cpp:353-361 unpack_exchange calls 'FixWallGranOld::unpack_exchange(nlocal,buf)' (which writes history_one on the host) and then modify_host() without the 'k_history_one.sync_host();' that its own pack_exchange does at :346 and that fix_spring_self_kokkos.cpp:318 does.
failure_scenario: a step where atoms leave a rank but none arrive (nrecv == 0 for every dimension): the device-side compaction is never registered, so the DualView still reports both sides in sync, and the next copy_arrays()/unpack_exchange() modify_host() makes the stale host copy authoritative - the compacted shear histories are lost.
suggested_fix: Add 'k_history_one.template modify<DeviceType>();' at the end of pack_exchange_kokkos, 'k_history_one.template sync<DeviceType>();' before the parallel_for in unpack_exchange_kokkos, and 'k_history_one.sync_host();' at the start of unpack_exchange.

summary: TagFixWallGranPackExchange computes the send-buffer offset as i*size_history from the atom's LOCAL index instead of the send-list slot mysend, while the buffer is only nsend*size_history long: the transmitted bytes are uninitialized and the write can run past the end of d_buf.
verified_by: orchestrator (src/KOKKOS/fix_wall_gran_kokkos.cpp:368-373; buffer length is nsend*size_history at :410. The correct convention is in fix_neigh_history_kokkos.cpp:378-391, which derives the offset from mysend/an explicit offset).

summary: TagFixWallGranUnpackExchange looks up index = d_indices(i) but then writes d_history_one(i,v) instead of d_history_one(index,v), so received shear history lands on the wrong atoms and the migrated atoms keep stale history.
verified_by: orchestrator (src/KOKKOS/fix_wall_gran_kokkos.cpp:418-425 vs the correct sibling fix_neigh_history_kokkos.cpp:459-471, which writes d_npartner(index)/d_partner(index,p)/d_valuepartner(index,...)).

summary: post_force's if/else chain covers only HOOKE (error), HOOKE_HISTORY and HERTZ_HISTORY (error); pairstyle GRANULAR falls through with neither a kernel nor an error, so the wall exerts no force at all. The HOOKE_HISTORY branch likewise has no REGION case, so wallstyle 'region' is silently a no-op.
verified_by: orchestrator (src/KOKKOS/fix_wall_gran_kokkos.cpp:105-119; the enums are fix_wall_gran_old.h:29 {HOOKE,HOOKE_HISTORY,HERTZ_HISTORY,GRANULAR} and fix_wall_gran_old.cpp:53 {...,ZCYLINDER,REGION}, both reachable from the parser at :84 and :379).

summary: FixWallGranKokkos::post_force() sets copymode = 1 and then takes an error->all() exit for the hooke / hertz/history wall styles, so copymode is never reset to 0 and every later destructor of the fix silently skips atom->delete_callback().
failure_scenario: Exception-enabled build (liblammps / the Python module, LAMMPS_EXCEPTIONS=on): `fix 1 all wall/gran/kk hooke 200000.0 NULL 50.0 NULL 0.5 0 zplane 0.0 NULL` then `run 1` -> post_force throws with copymode==1. The caller catches the exception and issues `unfix 1` (or any later fix/atom_style change): Modify::delete_fix destroys the fix, the destructors early-return, so the Atom GROW/RESTART callbacks for this fix are never removed and history_one/mass_rigid leak. The next atom->grow() dispatches grow_arrays() through the stale callback entry -> use-after-free / crash.
suggested_fix: Move both error->all() checks above `copymode = 1` (they only depend on pairstyle, which is fixed at construction), or reset copymode = 0 before erroring.

summary: pack_exchange_kokkos()/unpack_exchange_kokkos() ignore the ExecutionSpace argument and never mark/sync the exchange buffer (k_buf.modify<DeviceType>() + sync to the requested space), so with 'package kokkos comm/exchange host' on a GPU build the s_hist/t_hist of migrating atoms are packed into the device copy of the buffer while MPI sends the host copy.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/fix_qeq_reaxff_kokkos.cpp:1313-1343 'pack_exchange_kokkos(const int &nsend, DAT::tdual_double_2d_lr &k_buf, ..., ExecutionSpace /*space*/) { k_buf.sync<DeviceType>(); ... Kokkos::parallel_for(...TagQEqPackExchange...); ... k_s_hist.template modify<DeviceType>(); ... return nsend*nprev*2; }' -- no 'k_buf.modify<DeviceType>()' and no sync of k_buf; same in unpack_exchange_kokkos (:1362-1387). Every other KOKKOS fix does it, e.g. src/KOKKOS/fix_cmap_kokkos.cpp (pack_exchange_kokkos) 'k_buf.template modify<DeviceType>(); if (space == HostKK) k_buf.sync_host(); else k_buf.sync_device();', src/KOKKOS/fix_shake_kokkos.cpp and src/KOKKOS/fix_rigid_small_kokkos.cpp likewise. The caller src/KOKKOS/comm_kokkos.cpp:1373-1375 packs with 'kkbase->pack_exchange_kokkos(count,k_buf_send,...,ExecutionSpaceFromDevice<DeviceType>::space)' and then sends from 'MPI_Send(k_buf_send.view<DeviceType>().data(),nextrasend,...)' (:1404) where DeviceType is CommKokkos::exchange_device's template parameter -- LMPHostType when exchange_comm_on_host is set (src/KOKKOS/kokkos.cpp:589-591, 'package kokkos comm/exchange host'), while the fix's DeviceType is LMPDeviceType.
failure_scenario: GPU build with GPU-aware MPI, 'package kokkos comm/exchange host', pair_style reaxff/kk + fix qeq/reaxff/kk on >1 MPI rank: on every reneighboring step the charge-history (s_hist/t_hist) of every migrating atom is filled from whatever the host side of comm's send buffer last held, so the CG initial guess for those atoms is garbage (extra iterations, or non-convergence/NaN if the stale bytes are large).
suggested_fix: Add 'k_buf.template modify<DeviceType>(); if (space == HostKK) k_buf.sync_host(); else k_buf.sync_device();' at the end of pack_exchange_kokkos and sync k_buf from the space the data arrived in at the start of unpack_exchange_kokkos, as fix_cmap_kokkos.cpp / fix_shake_kokkos.cpp do.

summary: cg_solve() prints the non-convergence warning unconditionally, ignoring the documented 'nowarn' keyword (maxwarn) that the CPU style honors.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/fix_qeq_reaxff_kokkos.cpp:510-514: 'if (loop >= imax && comm->me == 0) error->warning(FLERR,fmt::format("Fix qeq/reaxff/kk cg_solve convergence failed after {} iterations at step {}: ..."));' vs src/REAXFF/fix_qeq_reaxff.cpp:812-814: 'if ((i >= imax) && maxwarn && (comm->me == 0)) error->warning(FLERR, "Fix qeq/reaxff CG convergence failed after {} iterations at step {}", i,update->ntimestep);'. maxwarn is set by the 'nowarn' keyword (src/REAXFF/fix_qeq_reaxff.cpp:77 'maxwarn = 1;' and :101 'else if (strcmp(arg[iarg],"nowarn") == 0) maxwarn = 0;') and is documented in doc/src/fix_qeq_reaxff.rst:87-92.
failure_scenario: fix 1 all qeq/reaxff/kk 1 0.0 10.0 1e-14 reaxff maxiter 20 nowarn -- the documented use case of forcing a fixed iteration count floods the log with one warning per QEq step instead of being silent.
suggested_fix: Add '&& maxwarn' to the condition, matching FixQEqReaxFF::CG().

summary: cg_solve() returns the fused loop count, so the global scalar of fix qeq/reaxff/kk is half of the value the CPU and OPENMP styles report for the same solve.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/fix_qeq_reaxff_kokkos.cpp:516 'return loop;' feeding :287 'matvecs = cg_solve();', with the inherited src/REAXFF/fix_qeq_reaxff.cpp:475-478 'double FixQEqReaxFF::compute_scalar() { return matvecs/2.0; }'. The CPU style counts both solves: src/REAXFF/fix_qeq_reaxff.cpp:626-628 'matvecs_s = CG(b_s, s); matvecs_t = CG(b_t, t); matvecs = matvecs_s + matvecs_t;', and the OPENMP fused solver does the same, src/OPENMP/fix_qeq_reaxff_omp.cpp:779-802 'matvecs_s = matvecs_t = i; ... return matvecs_s + matvecs_t;'.
failure_scenario: thermo_style custom step f_1 with fix qeq/reaxff vs fix qeq/reaxff/kk on the same input prints ~N and ~N/2 iterations respectively for an identical solve.
suggested_fix: Return 2*loop from cg_solve() (or set matvecs = 2*cg_solve()) so the reported scalar matches the CPU/OPENMP convention.

summary: get_chi_field() is called twice per QEq step (once from allocate_array(), once from pre_force()), and each call forces a device->host sync of x/mask/image plus a full host-side loop over all atoms.
evidence:
src/KOKKOS/fix_qeq_reaxff_kokkos.cpp:219 'allocate_array();' inside pre_force(), and allocate_array() ends with :360-364 '// init_storage
  if (efield) get_chi_field();
  Kokkos::parallel_for(...TagQEqZero...);'. pre_force() then repeats it at :265-267 '// init_matvec
  if (efield) get_chi_field();'. Each call is src/KOKKOS/fix_qeq_reaxff_kokkos.cpp:1430-1436 'atomKK->sync(Host,X_MASK|MASK_MASK|IMAGE_MASK); FixQEqReaxFF::get_chi_field(); k_chi_field.modify_host(); k_chi_field.sync_device();'. The CPU style calls it once per pre_force (src/REAXFF/fix_qeq_reaxff.cpp:622) plus once in init_storage(), which runs only from setup_pre_force().
failure_scenario: fix qeq/reaxff/kk together with fix efield on a GPU: every QEq step performs two full x/mask/image device->host copies and two O(nlocal) host loops instead of one.
suggested_fix: Drop the 'if (efield) get_chi_field();' from allocate_array() (the following TagQEqZero kernel only needs d_chi_field, which pre_force() refills right afterwards), or drop the duplicate call in pre_force().

summary: FixQEqReaxFFKokkos::init() syncs q to execution_space (Device) before FixQEqReaxFF::init() reads atom->q and atom->mask on the host, i.e. the sync is in the wrong direction and MASK_MASK is missing.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/fix_qeq_reaxff_kokkos.cpp:100-104: 'void FixQEqReaxFFKokkos<DeviceType>::init() { atomKK->sync(execution_space,Q_MASK); FixQEqReaxFF::init(); ...'. The only per-atom data the base init() touches is on the host: src/REAXFF/fix_qeq_reaxff.cpp:422-427 'double qsum_local = 0.0, qsum = 0.0; for (int i = 0; i < atom->nlocal; i++) { if (atom->mask[i] & groupbit) qsum_local += atom->q[i]; } MPI_Allreduce(...)'. With execution_space == Device, atomKK->sync(Device,Q_MASK) copies host->device (a no-op when the device copy is the fresh one) and leaves the host copy stale.
failure_scenario: Two consecutive run commands with fix qeq/reaxff/kk on a GPU: the first run leaves q modified on the device (fix_qeq_reaxff_kokkos.cpp:537 'atomKK->modified(execution_space,Q_MASK)'); the second run's init() then computes qsum from the pre-run host charges and prints (or fails to print) the 'group is not charge neutral' warning based on stale data.
suggested_fix: Change the call to 'atomKK->sync(Host, Q_MASK|MASK_MASK);' since the base init() reads those arrays on the host.

summary: The H-matrix capacity reduction sums d_numneigh[ii] over the list index ii instead of d_numneigh[d_ilist[ii]], while every consumer of that capacity indexes by d_ilist[ii]; the two agree only because the Kokkos neighbor build happens to set d_ilist(i)==i.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/fix_qeq_reaxff_kokkos.cpp:1453-1456: 'void FixQEqReaxFFKokkosNeighborFunctor<DeviceType>::operator()(TagQEqNeighborNumNeigh, const int& ii, bigint& totneigh) const { totneigh += static_cast<bigint>(d_numneigh[ii]); }' -- the result is m_cap_big (:230-231) and sizes d_jlist/d_val (:326-327). Both consumers dereference the ilist first: the CPU scan at :1487-1497 'const int i = d_ilist[ii]; ... const int jnum = d_numneigh[i];' and the GPU team version at :1592-1600 'const int i = d_ilist[ii]; int jnum = d_numneigh[i]; ... totalnbrs += jnum;' whose per-team total is reserved with 'Kokkos::atomic_fetch_add(&d_mfill_offset(), totalnbrs)' (:1618). The CPU base sums the same way as the consumers: src/REAXFF/fix_qeq_reaxff.cpp:374-378 'm = 0; for (ii = 0; ii < nn; ii++) { i = ilist[ii]; m += numneigh[i]; }'. Today src/KOKKOS/npair_kokkos.cpp:593,838,970,1132,1330,1575 all set 'neigh_list.d_ilist(i) = i;', so the two sums are equal and no overrun occurs.
failure_scenario: Latent: if any Kokkos neighbor build ever produces a non-identity or subset d_ilist (e.g. a reordered or partial ilist), the GPU team compute_H reserves more slots than m_cap_big and writes past the end of d_jlist/d_val (out-of-bounds device write, silent corruption).
suggested_fix: Change the functor to 'totneigh += static_cast<bigint>(d_numneigh[d_ilist[ii]]);' so the capacity estimate matches the consumers and the CPU base.

summary: fix qeq/reaxff/kk declares X_MASK in datamask_modify although it never writes atom positions, and omits the Q_MASK it does write.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/fix_qeq_reaxff_kokkos.cpp:64-65 `datamask_read = X_MASK | V_MASK | F_MASK | Q_MASK | MASK_MASK | TYPE_MASK | TAG_MASK; datamask_modify = X_MASK;`, and line 307 `atomKK->modified(execution_space,datamask_modify);`.  The style only reads x (`x(i,0)` etc. at lines 742-744 and in the neighbor kernels); the array it actually writes is q (line 1002 `q(i) = ...`), which is claimed separately at line 537 `atomKK->modified(execution_space,Q_MASK);`.  Compare the sibling src/KOKKOS/fix_acks2_reaxff_kokkos.cpp:60 `datamask_modify = Q_MASK | X_MASK;` -- the same spurious X_MASK, but there Q_MASK is at least declared.
failure_scenario: No wrong numbers: marking the device x newer right after the same hook synced it only costs a redundant device-to-host copy of x on the next host access.  It is a datamask/actual-access mismatch, the exact thing the KOKKOS rules require to agree, and it hides the fact that Q_MASK is missing from the declaration.
suggested_fix: Set `datamask_modify = Q_MASK;` (dropping X_MASK), which also makes the explicit modified(Q_MASK) at line 537 redundant rather than load-bearing.

summary: GroupKokkos::angmom_kk() uses the raw atom velocity instead of the deformation-corrected velocity, so with 'fix deform ... remap v' the angular momentum differs from Group::angmom() by the h_rate image term.
failure_scenario: 'fix deform ... remap v' together with 'fix momentum N group angular' (src/KOKKOS/fix_momentum_kokkos.cpp:135 calls angmom_kk) or 'fix addtorque/group' (src/KOKKOS/fix_addtorque_group_kokkos.cpp:98): for any atom of the deform group with a nonzero image flag the velocity used is the peculiar velocity instead of the streaming-corrected one, so the removed/applied angular momentum is wrong and the /kk run silently disagrees with the same input run without -k on.
suggested_fix: Add a DomainKokkos::unmap overload that also returns the corrected velocity (taking h_rate, deform_vremap and deform_groupbit as captured scalars) and use it in angmom_kk, matching Domain::unmap(x,v,image,mask,y,u).

summary: vcm_kk() forms the momentum products in KK_FLOAT (float in single/mixed precision) before widening to the double accumulator, unlike every other reduction in the same file and unlike Group::vcm().
failure_scenario: A mixed-precision KOKKOS build (KOKKOS_PRECISION=mixed) running 'fix momentum linear' or 'compute temp/com' (src/KOKKOS/compute_temp_com_kokkos.cpp:57): each term of the center-of-mass velocity is rounded to float before summation, so the removed drift and the temperature bias carry single-precision error even though the accumulator is double.
suggested_fix: Cast d_v(i,*) and massone to double before multiplying, as the other kernels in this header do.

verified_by: orchestrator (read code directly); found by group 06
summary: GroupKokkos::angmom_kk() uses the raw velocity where Group::angmom() uses Domain::unmap's deformation-corrected velocity (h_rate image term); the KOKKOS header never reads h_rate/deform_vremap.
evidence: group_kokkos.h:378-384 and 402-408 use d_v directly; grep h_rate/deform_vremap group_kokkos.h: none; src/group.cpp:1503-1513 and src/domain.cpp:1960-1966.
failure_scenario: fix deform remap v + fix momentum angular (or fix addtorque/group) on a GPU: wrong angular momentum for atoms of the deform group with nonzero image flags.
suggested_fix: Add a DomainKokkos unmap overload returning the corrected velocity and use it in angmom_kk.

summary: memset_kokkos() keeps its zeroing functor in a function-local static and zeroes only floor(bytes/4) bytes; the helper is dead code (no caller anywhere in src/).
evidence: src/KOKKOS/kokkos_type.h:1421-1427: 'template<class ViewType> void memset_kokkos (ViewType &view) { static MemsetZeroFunctor<typename ViewType::execution_space> f; f.ptr = view.data(); Kokkos::parallel_for(view.span()*sizeof(typename ViewType::value_type)/4, f); ... }'. The functor object is shared by every call for a given execution space, and 'f.ptr' is written before the launch, so two host threads calling this for different views race on 'f.ptr'. The trip count 'span()*sizeof(value_type)/4' truncates: a view whose byte size is not a multiple of 4 leaves its last 1-3 bytes untouched. 'grep -rn memset_kokkos src/' finds only this definition -- there is no caller.
failure_scenario: If a future caller uses it on a view whose byte size is not a multiple of 4 (e.g. a char or a 2-byte value type), the tail bytes stay uninitialized; if two threads call it concurrently one view is zeroed twice and the other not at all.
suggested_fix: Delete the unused helper, or replace its body with 'Kokkos::deep_copy(view, typename ViewType::value_type());' which is correct for any value type and has no shared state.

summary: Two blocks of commented-out code left in the header, which the project coding rules ask to remove.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/kokkos_type.h:185 '//typedef Kokkos::LayoutLeft LMPDeviceLayout;' inside the '#else' of the layout selection, and src/KOKKOS/kokkos_type.h:1465 '//typedef struct { SNAreal re, im; } SNAcomplex;' just above the SNAComplex template.
failure_scenario: None at runtime; the review checklist in .github/copilot-instructions.md ('Commented out code ... should be removed entirely') flags these.
suggested_fix: Delete both commented-out typedefs.

summary: The 'if (SINGLE_DEVICE) modify_legacy_device();' branch inside TransformView::sync_hostkk_to_legacy() is unreachable, because a single-device Kokkos DualView always reports need_sync_host()/need_sync_device() as false.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/kokkos_type.h:1041-1049: 'if (modified_hostkk_legacy) { Kokkos::deep_copy(h_view,h_viewkk); modified_hostkk_legacy = 0; if (k_view.need_sync_host() || k_view.need_sync_device()) { if (SINGLE_DEVICE) modify_legacy_device(); } else modified_legacy_device = 0; }'. SINGLE_DEVICE is defined at line 714 as 't_dev::device_type == t_host::device_type', which is exactly Kokkos' impl_dualview_is_single_device; for such a DualView Kokkos' need_sync<Device>() returns false unconditionally, so the guarded call can never execute and the else branch always runs under SINGLE_DEVICE.
failure_scenario: No wrong results today; the intent of the branch (record that the legacy host is now ahead of the device) is silently never carried out, so a later change to the surrounding logic will behave differently from what the code reads as.
suggested_fix: Drop the dead 'if (SINGLE_DEVICE)' branch, or if the intent was the non-single-device case, change it to 'if (!SINGLE_DEVICE) modify_legacy_device();' and re-verify the sync state machine.

summary: Same d_flag race as bond_fene_kokkos: plain stores of 2 (fatal) and 1 (warning) to one shared scalar can hide a 'Bad FENE bond' abort.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/bond_fene_expand_kokkos.cpp:191-197 'if (rlogarg < 0.1) { if (rlogarg <= -3.0) d_flag() = 2; else d_flag() = 1; rlogarg = 0.1; }' and :135-138 'if (h_flag() == 1) error->warning(...); else if (h_flag() == 2) error->one(FLERR,"Bad FENE bond");'. CPU base src/MOLECULE/bond_fene_expand.cpp:87-92 aborts per-bond via 'if (rlogarg <= -3.0) error->one(FLERR, "Bad FENE bond");'.
failure_scenario: Two bonds in the same kernel launch, one with rlogarg <= -3.0 and one with -3.0 < rlogarg < 0.1: the fatal flag can be overwritten by the warning flag and the run continues with the bond clamped to rlogarg = 0.1.
suggested_fix: Replace the plain stores with Kokkos::atomic_max on d_flag() so the severity is monotone.

summary: allocate_kokkos() calls DualView::resize() without first forcing the host copy to be the newest, so on a GPU build a dihedral_coeff issued after a run (when the dual views are in the 'device up to date' state) silently zeroes the host mirror and then that zeroed mirror is copied back over the device coefficients.
failure_scenario: GPU build (host and device memory spaces differ). Input: 'dihedral_style fourier/kk; dihedral_coeff 1 2 ...; dihedral_coeff 2 2 ...; run 100; dihedral_coeff 3 4 ... (nterms_max grows from 2 to 4); run 100'. In the second run all dihedral types except type 3 have k/cos_shift/sin_shift/multiplicity = 0, so their dihedral energies and forces silently become zero.
suggested_fix: Call sync_host()/modify_host() (or simply k_*.sync_host() followed by modify_host()) on each dual view before resizing, or pass Kokkos::view_alloc(Kokkos::SequentialHostInit) / reallocate and refill all types after a resize, so the host mirror is authoritative when resize() runs.

summary: improper distharm/kk drops the six domain->minimum_image() calls the CPU ImproperDistHarm::compute applies to its bond vectors, so plane normal, projection and forces differ from the base style when a bond vector exceeds half the box.
evidence: CPU src/YAFF/improper_distharm.cpp:98-131 folds every difference vector: `xab = x[i2][0] - x[i1][0]; ... domain->minimum_image(FLERR, xab,yab,zab);` and likewise for xac (:107), xad (:113), xbc (:119), xbd (:125) and xcd (:131). The KOKKOS kernel src/KOKKOS/improper_distharm_kokkos.cpp:149-167 forms the same differences (`const KK_FLOAT xab = x(i2,0) - x(i1,0); ... const KK_FLOAT zcd = x(i4,2) - x(i3,2);`) with no folding; `grep -n minimum_image src/KOKKOS/improper_distharm_kokkos.cpp` is empty and domain.h is not included. Everything else in the kernel (xna/yna/zna, rna, da = -(xna*xad+...), domega, a, f1..f4 at :188-208) matches CPU :133-169 term for term. src/KOKKOS/bond_harmonic_restrain_kokkos.cpp:111-121 and :243-295 show the device-side minimum_image pattern already used in this package.
failure_scenario: improper_style distharm vs distharm/kk in a periodic cell whose shortest edge is under twice an improper bond length (or an improper wrapped across a boundary): the CPU folds xbc/xcd/xad before building the plane normal and the projection da, the /kk style does not, giving different energy k*(da-chi)^2 and different forces on all four atoms.
suggested_fix: Copy domain->triclinic/xprd/yprd/zprd/*_half into the functor in compute() and apply a KOKKOS_INLINE_FUNCTION minimum_image() to the difference vectors, as in src/KOKKOS/bond_harmonic_restrain_kokkos.cpp:243-295.

summary: ThirdOrderKokkos::setup() shadows the non-virtual ThirdOrder::setup(), so the KOKKOS version is never executed.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/third_order_kokkos.h declares `void setup();` without `override`; src/PHONON/third_order.h:23 declares `void setup();` NON-virtual while lines 37-39 declare `virtual void update_force(); virtual void force_clear(); virtual void openfile(...)`. Callers are src/PHONON/third_order.cpp:186 and :194 inside ThirdOrder::command(); src/KOKKOS/third_order_kokkos.cpp:79-83 ThirdOrderKokkos::command() just syncs and calls ThirdOrder::command(narg,arg). ThirdOrderKokkos::setup() (third_order_kokkos.cpp:91-135) with `lmp->kokkos->auto_sync = 1;` (line 93), the pair_compute_flag sync/compute/modified block (lines 117-123) and `auto_sync = 0` (line 126) is dead code.
failure_scenario: `third_order all ... ` run with -k on -sf kk: the CPU ThirdOrder::setup() runs, auto_sync is never enabled around the host-side domain/comm/neighbor block, so host x/image data can be stale on a GPU run and the third-order force constants come out wrong.
suggested_fix: Make ThirdOrder::setup() virtual in src/PHONON/third_order.h:23 and add `override` to the KOKKOS declaration (same fix as dynamical_matrix).

summary: NBinSSAKokkos allocates and initializes d_resize/h_resize and declares c_binID/c_bins/c_gbins, none of which are ever read by anything.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/nbin_ssa_kokkos.h:48 'typename AT::t_int_1d_const c_binID;' (never assigned), :55 'c_bins' and :62 'c_gbins' (assigned only at src/KOKKOS/nbin_ssa_kokkos.cpp:196 'c_gbins = gbins;' and :224 'c_bins = bins;'), :64-65 'd_resize'/'h_resize' (allocated at nbin_ssa_kokkos.cpp:38/45 and set at :52 'h_resize() = 1;', then never touched again).  The consumer keeps its own copies: src/KOKKOS/npair_ssa_kokkos.cpp:87-93 takes only atoms_per_bin, k_bincount, k_bins, ghosts_per_gbin, k_gbincount and k_gbins, and npair_ssa_kokkos.h:136 declares its own c_gbins.  Note also that npair_ssa_kokkos.cpp:87/91 copy atoms_per_bin and ghosts_per_gbin into members that are themselves never used.
failure_scenario: No runtime effect; dead state that makes the class larger and misleads readers into thinking there is a resize/retry protocol like the one in NBinKokkos.
suggested_fix: Delete the unused members (and the corresponding allocations in the constructor and the two assignments in bin_atoms()).

summary: setup_tables() unconditionally copies tb->de, tb->df and tb->f into device views, but for tabstyle spline those arrays are never filled by DihedralTable::compute_table(), so the copy reads uninitialized heap memory.
evidence: src/KOKKOS/dihedral_table_cut_kokkos.cpp:467-474 `for (int i = 0; i < tablength; i++) { ... k_de.view_host()(m,i) = static_cast<KK_FLOAT>(tb->de[i]); k_f_tab.view_host()(m,i) = static_cast<KK_FLOAT>(tb->f[i]); k_df.view_host()(m,i) = static_cast<KK_FLOAT>(tb->df[i]); ... }`.  src/MOLECULE/dihedral_table.cpp:1113-1119 allocates these with memory->create (no initialization) and fills de/df only in the `else if (tabstyle == LINEAR)` branch (:1131-1164).  src/EXTRA-MOLECULE/dihedral_table_cut.cpp:~1295 states it explicitly: "If the user did not specify the forces now, AND the user selected the spline option ... THEN the tb->f array is uninitialized".
failure_scenario: dihedral_style table/cut spline N ... with a NOF table: setup_tables reads ntables*tablength uninitialized doubles (de, df, f). The kernel never uses them in the spline branch, so results are correct, but it is an uninitialized read (valgrind/MSan) and narrowing garbage doubles to float in a single-precision KOKKOS build is undefined behaviour.
suggested_fix: Guard the copies: only fill k_de/k_df when tabstyle == LINEAR and k_f_tab/k_f2 when !tb->f_unspecified, or zero those arrays in DihedralTable::compute_table().

summary: For special-bonded (factor_coul<1) core/shell pairs the Buckingham term is evaluated with 1/(rsq+EPSILON) instead of the CPU style's 1/(rsq+EPS_EWALD_SQR), so the vdW force/energy of such a pair differs from the CPU reference.
evidence: src/CORESHELL/pair_buck_coul_long_cs.cpp:105 'rsq += EPSILON;' then 124 'r2inv = 1.0/(rsq + EPS_EWALD_SQR);' inside the factor_coul<1 branch, and 150-156 use that r2inv for r6inv, forcebuck AND fpair.  src/KOKKOS/pair_buck_coul_long_cs_kokkos.cpp:194 'const KK_FLOAT rsq = rsq_in + static_cast<KK_FLOAT>(EPSILON);' (compute_fpair) and 221 the same in compute_evdwl always use EPSILON=1e-20, never EPS_EWALD_SQR=1e-12; the EPS_EWALD_SQR correction is applied only inside compute_fcoul (line 286 'return forcecoul / (rsq_cs + EPS_EWALD_SQR);').
failure_scenario: pair_style buck/coul/long/cs/kk with a core/shell pair at r -> 0 that has special_coul<1 but special_lj != 0: the CPU caps r2inv at 1e12 while the KOKKOS style uses 1e20, so r6inv differs by 24 orders of magnitude; for ordinary separations the difference is ~1e-12 relative.
suggested_fix: Pass the same effective r2inv to the vdW terms, e.g. add EPS_EWALD_SQR (not EPSILON) in compute_fpair/compute_evdwl when factor_coul<1, mirroring the CPU r2inv reassignment.

summary: The 'Accelerator Variant' lines of dynamical_matrix.rst and third_order.rst name the KOKKOS style without the *...* emphasis markers used by every other one of the 275 doc pages that carry such a line.
evidence:
doc/src/dynamical_matrix.rst:7:
  Accelerator Variant: dynamical_matrix/kk
doc/src/third_order.rst:7:
  Accelerator Variant: third_order/kk
compare doc/src/region.rst:6:
  Accelerator Variants: *block/kk*, *cone/kk*, *cylinder/kk*, *ellipsoid/kk*, *plane/kk*, *prism/kk*, *sphere/kk*
and doc/src/fix_efield.rst:11:
  Accelerator Variant: *efield/kk*
A scan of all doc/src/*.rst 'Accelerator Variant' lines finds these two as the only entries whose style name is not italicised.
failure_scenario: Cosmetic only: the two command pages render the KOKKOS style name in body text rather than as an emphasised style name, and a grep/regex over the docs for '\*<style>/kk\*' (the pattern used by tooling and by this audit) misses them.
suggested_fix: Write 'Accelerator Variant: *dynamical_matrix/kk*' and 'Accelerator Variant: *third_order/kk*'.
